narrative.title: Ridge Detection on a Grid Elevation Model
narrative.scenario: A terrain model stores one elevation per cell, with no two adjacent cells equal, and surveyors need a summit - a cell higher than its four direct neighbours. Cells past the border count as a drop to -1. Binary searching the rows and comparing each row's best cell against its vertical neighbours finds a summit without scanning the whole grid.
narrative.inputFormat: An m x n matrix mat with no two adjacent cells equal.
narrative.outputFormat: A two-element array [row, col] of any peak cell, where the cell is strictly greater than its existing left, right, top and bottom neighbours.
constraints: No two adjacent cells are equal
An O(m log n) or O(n log m) algorithm is required

testCases.explanation: Both 4 and 3 exceed all their neighbours; this profile reports the position of 4.
The cell 30 beats 20, 21, 14 and 16, so it is a valid summit.

hintLevels: Level 1: Pick the tallest cell in a row and you only have to worry about its top and bottom neighbours - left and right are already beaten.
Level 2: Binary search the row index; at each probe, find that row's maximum column and compare upward and downward to decide which half holds a summit.
Level 3: Row ends and grid borders must be guarded so out-of-range comparisons never fire, and a peak is guaranteed to exist because no two adjacent cells are equal.
